**Evidence** (43 quoted fields), by checklist area:

#### cache-challenges · Identity and id

- `self_description` · [S1][cache-challenges-s1]
  > a public benchmarking project to compare and improve small molecule hit-finding algorithms through cycles of prediction and experimental testing
- `released` = 2021-12-01 · [S2][cache-challenges-s2]
  > Application opens 2021-12-01

#### cache-challenges · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary chemistry-materials/experimental-hit-finding · [S3][cache-challenges-s3]
  - why: Teams nominate compounds for a protein target, the organisers procure them and test them in the laboratory, and each team is scored on what those experiments return, which is the leaf's definition and the case the family's exclusion test names.
  > CACHE will procure the molecules from commercial vendors and test them experimentally with two rigorous binding assays.
- `capability` = hypothesis-generation · [S4][cache-challenges-s4]
  - why: Each team's output is a set of candidates, up to 100 nominated compounds and then up to 50 analogues of its hits, and the challenge scores that set by the hits confirmed in it.
  > CACHE Challenges begin with a hit-finding round (Round 1), where participants can nominate up to 100 commercially available compounds.
- `capability` = creativity-novelty · [S5][cache-challenges-s5]
  - why: The Hit Evaluation Committee scores chemical novelty against previously disclosed compounds, and challenges on targets with known ligands ask for new scaffolds (Challenge #4 against the patent series) or exclude a known chemotype (Challenge #7's quinazolines).
  > the Committee evaluated any chemical liability and chemical novelty compared with previously disclosed compounds
- `capability` = scientific-prediction · [S6][cache-challenges-s6]
  - why: Participants predict which molecules bind the target, and the score compares those predictions with binding measured in the organisers' assays.
  > Participants will predict hits and CACHE will validate these hits experimentally.
- `capability` = search-exploration · [S7][cache-challenges-s7]
  - why: Teams search commercial catalogues of billions of compounds with a fixed budget of up to 100 nominations each, and hit rate, discovery under that budget, is what separates the workflows.
  > While most hit rates were between 0 and 3%
- `evaluation_method` = wet-lab-validation, human-expert-eval · [S3][cache-challenges-s3]
  - why: The nominated compounds are bought and assayed after submission, and the measured binding is the ground truth. Experts then score the outcome compound by compound (human-expert-eval) - in Challenges #2 and #5 the Hit Evaluation Committee assigns a score to each Round 1 hit, blind to the participant, and workflows are compared by their best and summed hit scores (task.blinding).
  > CACHE will procure the molecules from commercial vendors and test them experimentally with two rigorous binding assays.
- `designed_for_subjects` = human-ai-team, domain-specialist-model, classical-algorithm · [S7][cache-challenges-s7]
  - why: The entrant is a team's workflow. Many workflows rest on neural networks trained for chemistry tasks (learned\_entrant\_evidence), others are purely physics-based docking and scoring, and teams choose the final compounds by hand after computing; the quoted Challenge #2 workflow is both the second and the third.
  > WF1448 used purely physics-based approaches for docking (Glide) and Scoring (HYDE), followed by visual inspection and selection of top compounds by both computational and medicinal chemists.

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `chemistry-materials/generative-molecular-design` · [S3][cache-challenges-s3]
  - why: Some workflows design new molecules, which their teams must have made, but most nominations are picked from commercial catalogues and the score is the assay, not a stated property specification.
  > Compounds from de novo design methods will be procured by participants

#### cache-challenges · Task and evaluation

- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system the ten CACHE #2 teams whose workflows used neural networks · [S7][cache-challenges-s7]
  > Out of 23 teams, ten used neural networks to generate or evaluate compounds
- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system the seven successful CACHE #1 workflows, five of them with deep-learning steps · [S9][cache-challenges-s9]
  > five used one or more deep learning steps
- `ground_truth_source` = experimental · [S4][cache-challenges-s4]
  > Primary screening of nominated compounds was conducted by SPR, an assay that measures direct binding of compounds to the WDR domain of LRRK2 captured on a chip.
- `reproducible_by_third_party` = false · [S4][cache-challenges-s4]
  - why: A score exists only once the organisers have bought the compounds, run the assays and had the committee judge the results. The compounds and the data are released afterwards, so the measurements can be repeated, but not the blind prediction they scored.
  > All CACHE#1 compounds were tested experimentally at the Structural Genomics Consortium, University of Toronto
- `task.blinding` · [S5][cache-challenges-s5]
  > Each compound was assigned a score by a panel of medicinal chemistry and GPCR biophysics experts (the IDs of participants were blinded).
- `task` = exists true; input the challenge's protein target, with whatever it comes with -- structures of the site, known ligands from the literature or patents, fragment or DNA-encoded-library screening data, a commercial compound catalogue, mostly Enamine's, from which nominations must be purchasable; output Up to 100 nominated compounds in the hit-finding round and up to 50 analogues in the hit-expansion round, plus, in a separate exercise, a prediction of which compounds are active in the pooled library of every team's first-round nominations.; scoring The organisers procure and assay the nominated compounds; an independent Hit Evaluation Committee scores each confirmed hit on its measured activity, its chemistry and its novelty, and on how its analogues behaved. Workflows are then compared by their best hit score, by the summed score of all their hits, and by their score on the pooled library.; tests_hidden_from_system true · [S5][cache-challenges-s5]
  > A second metric is the aggregated score (i.e. sum of all scores) across all confirmed hits predicted by a workflow which better reflects hit rate.
- `execution.compute_tier` = participant-funded-procurement · [S10][cache-challenges-s10]
  - why: What an entrant pays for is the physical compounds the organisers then assay, which is the term's inclusion test and the case the vocabulary cites this benchmark for; the bench work is recorded as a blocker instead.
  > CACHE will cover 100% of the costs of testing compounds experimentally. 100% of the costs of procuring compounds (either make-on-demand or custom-synthesized compounds) will be covered by participants.
- `execution.reproducibility_tier` = requires-physical-experiment · [S1][cache-challenges-s1]
  - why: Producing a score means buying compounds, running binding assays with orthogonal confirmation and convening medicinal chemists to judge the result. The compounds and the data are released at the end of each challenge, so the measurements themselves are repeatable by a laboratory; what cannot be repeated is the blind prediction, which the live-world-state blocker records.
  > Each compound will be assayed at a single concentration in duplicate, and each positive will be re-tested in dose-response mode, as well as in an orthogonal biophysical assay
- `aggregation_policy` = official-aggregate · [S5][cache-challenges-s5]
  > A second metric is the aggregated score (i.e. sum of all scores) across all confirmed hits predicted by a workflow which better reflects hit rate.

- `lifecycle` = active · [S6][cache-challenges-s6]

**Open review checks** (11):

1. (field `versions`) One entry for the series, with the eight challenges as editions. Each challenge has its own target, assays, activity threshold and field of teams, and the scores do not compare across them, so each could instead be its own entry, as the corpus treats some yearly challenges.
2. (field `versions`) The DREAM x CACHE Target 2035 Challenge is listed in the same site menu, shares the CACHE Terms of Participation and is supported by Conscience, but it is run with the SGC, Sage Bionetworks and IBM's DREAM on Synapse, with a retrospective phase before the prospective one. It is excluded here and may deserve its own entry. · [S6][cache-challenges-s6]
   > with logistical and technical support from Conscience and BEACON
3. (field `evaluation_method`) human-expert-eval against expert-panel-assessment. The Hit Evaluation Committee scores each confirmed hit and the results pages rank workflows from those scores, which the panel term's exclusion sends to human-expert-eval; but Challenge #1's page says the committee's work led to a final score per participant, which is the panel term's own case. · [S4][cache-challenges-s4]
   > leading to a final score assigned to each participant
4. (field `evaluation_target`) evaluation\_target: mixed is the first in this corpus; every other entry is learned-system. The field of entrants holds neural-network workflows, purely physics-based ones and human selection in both. · [S7][cache-challenges-s7]
   > Out of 23 teams, ten used neural networks to generate or evaluate compounds
5. (field `activity`) activity results-pending against between-rounds. No call for applications is open and the open challenges are being assayed and scored, but Challenge #5's final results are published, so a reader could call the series between rounds instead.
6. (field `execution.reproducibility_tier`, needs a specialist) reproducibility\_tier requires-physical-experiment, where 02 S12.4 proposed not-independently-reproducible. The assays and the released compounds can be repeated by a laboratory; the blind round cannot, which is recorded as the live-world-state blocker.
7. (field `governance.maintainer_type`) maintainer\_type nonprofit against consortium. Conscience holds and runs the challenges, but a Governing Board of industry representatives decides the course of each one and the SGC runs the experiments; no source read here gives that board a legal form. · [S11][cache-challenges-s11]
   > The Governing Board for CACHE consists of representatives from industry that make various decisions on the course of each CACHE Challenge.
8. (field `governance.independence_flags`) funded-by-evaluated-party rests on the design paper's statement that the SGC, which runs the assays, is funded by pharmaceutical companies, beside a Merck KGaA team placing third in Challenge #1. Whether funding the experimental hub counts as funding the benchmark is a reviewer's call. · [S4][cache-challenges-s4]
   > \[withheld: it may name a person; see the entry file\]
9. (field `data.dataset_licence`) The released structures and assay data carry no named licence, only the promise that they are unrestricted; dataset\_licence is null rather than a guess. The website's own CC BY 4.0 footer covers the pages, not the data.
10. (field `ground_truth_source`, needs a specialist) The assay conditions recorded here are Challenges #1, #2 and #5's. The pipeline changes with the target -- SPR and ITC or 19F NMR for the structural-biology targets, a radioligand competition assay and a cellular functional assay for the GPCR, an enzyme assay where the target is an enzyme -- so a per-edition assay record would be better than one summary.
11. (field `versions`) The Challenge #4 results paper (J Chem Inf Model, 2026-11-13, DOI 10.1021/acs.jcim.6c02396; on 2026-11-17 the publications page listed its ChemRxiv preprint, DOI 10.26434/chemrxiv.15005792) and the Challenge #3 one (DOI 10.1021/acs.jcim.5c02441) were not read, because chemrxiv.org and pubs.acs.org refused this project's fetcher. versions\[challenge-3\] and \[challenge-4\] cite only the listing, and their changes text still rests on the news and home pages. Read from the papers, the team and compound counts, the activity thresholds and the hit counts should be checked. · [S12][cache-challenges-s12]
   > \[withheld: it may name a person; see the entry file\]

**Reviewer checklist** for `cache-challenges`:

- [ ] Identity and id: the name, aliases, id, paper and release date are right, and this is one benchmark, not a family or an edition of another
- [ ] Domain and capabilities: the primary and secondary subdomains, capabilities, evaluation methods and intended subjects fit, and no rejected term should have been kept
- [ ] Task and evaluation: the task, scoring, ground truth, entrants and harness read as the sources describe them
- [ ] Data and licence: access, refresh, provenance, sizes, subsets, contamination and licences match the sources
- [ ] Governance and independence: maintainer type, submission process, funding and independence flags are right
- [ ] Lifecycle and activity: lifecycle, activity, versions, editions and history are current
- [ ] Every open review check above is answered or resolved
- [ ] Nothing here would embarrass the catalogue in front of a specialist
